title: Live imaging of the Drosophila ovarian germline stem cell niche
author: Wilcockson, Ashe
materials: Leica TCS SP8 AOBS inverted microscope
FluoroDish cell culture dish 35 mm, 10 mm well
The niche cells cannot be located.
No new materials were generated for this study.

steps.title: Prepare fly stocks
steps.instruction: Maintain all Drosophila lines at 18 °C for long‑term storage and at 25 °C for crosses. Raise flies on standard food (50 g L⁻¹ yeast, 78 g L⁻¹ glucose, 72 g L⁻¹ maize flour, 8 g L⁻¹ agar, 27 mL L⁻¹ nipagin, 3 mL L⁻¹ propionic acid). Transfer 20–30 virgin females and 5–10 males of the nos‑Gal4::VP16, UASp‑eGFP‑αTubulin84B line (BDSC_7253) to a fresh vial with yeast paste, keep at 25 °C and flip to a new vial daily. Keep the old vials at 25 °C to collect emerging virgin females and young males for experimental crosses. If combining additional reporters (e.g., UASp‑RNAi), first establish balanced double‑ or multi‑transgenic stocks.

steps.title: Maintain experimental females
steps.instruction: Set up a cross of 20–30 virgin females with 5–10 males in a vial containing standard food at 25 °C. Transfer flies to a fresh vial every 1–2 days until dissection (typically 3–5 days) to ensure mating and healthy reproduction without aging effects. Optional: supplement food with dry yeast to boost reproduction. If using RNAi or other transgenes that may affect male fertility, keep only wild‑type males with the experimental females. Temperature can be altered (e.g., 29 °C) to enhance RNAi knockdown, but must be empirically determined for each experiment.

steps.title: Prepare supplemented insect media
steps.instruction: Supplement Schneider’s Drosophila medium with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin to create SIM stock. From SIM make two additional stocks: (a) add fibrinogen to a final concentration of 10 mg mL⁻¹ → fSIM (aliquot and store at –20 °C); (b) add human insulin to a final concentration of 200 µg mL⁻¹ → iSIM (prepare fresh on the day of use).

steps.title: Pre‑heat media for dissection
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat 5 mL of SIM, 1 mL of fSIM and 2 mL of iSIM to 37 °C. This prevents fibrinogen precipitation in fSIM and avoids temperature shocks during washing and mounting.

steps.title: Set up dissection wells
steps.instruction: In a 6‑well plate or glass dissection dish arrange: three wells each containing 500 µL pre‑warmed SIM for fly washes, two wells (on a glass dish) each with 500 µL SIM for dissection, and one well with 200 µL pre‑warmed fSIM for later mounting.

steps.title: Anesthetize and euthanize flies
steps.instruction: Anesthetize flies by CO₂ puffing or by placing the vial on ice (4 °C) for 5 min or until they settle at the bottom. Take 2–3 females, being careful they do not stick in the yeast paste. Euthanize by submerging flies in 70 % ethanol for exactly 1 min, avoiding damage to the abdomen or prolonged exposure.

steps.title: Wash and dissect ovaries
steps.instruction: Transfer flies to the first three SIM wash wells, shaking gently for 1 min in each well. Move flies to the fourth SIM well and dissect all ovaries: turn the female on her back, pull the ovipositor with forceps to remove the posterior abdomen; if ovaries stay attached, lightly pinch the abdomen to release them.

steps.title: Microdissect ovarioles and remove muscle
steps.instruction: Place dissected ovaries in a final SIM well for microdissection. Using an eyelash tool (eyelash glued to a toothpick with nail varnish), comb through the ovaries to break the overlying muscle sheath and tease individual ovarioles. Sever any remaining sheath at the anterior terminal filament or posterior egg chamber with the eyelash tool or fine scissors, removing as much muscle as possible. Select only ovarioles that detach easily to avoid mechanical stress.

steps.title: Transfer ovarioles to fibrinogen solution
steps.instruction: Pipette 5–10 ovarioles in 10 µL SIM into the well containing 200 µL pre‑warmed fSIM. Then pipette the 5–10 µL fSIM‑containing ovarioles onto a 35 mm FluoroDish (glass‑bottom) and spread the droplet thinly with the eyelash tool, positioning ovarioles close together (optional, for easier locating).

steps.title: Mount ovarioles and add thrombin
steps.instruction: Add 1–2 µL of thrombin (10 U mL⁻¹) dropwise to the fSIM droplet (add 0.5 µL at a time) to initiate fibrinogen‑thrombin clot formation. Minimize contact between the pipette tip and the media to prevent premature clotting on the tip. Cover the FluoroDish and incubate for 10 min at 20 °C to allow the clot to solidify (opacity increase indicates completion).

steps.title: Add insulin media and prevent drying
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of iSIM pre‑warmed to 25 °C onto the clot. Place a piece of damp tissue paper at the dish edge to keep the preparation from drying out.

steps.title: Configure confocal microscope
steps.instruction: Set up a Leica TCS SP8 AOBS inverted confocal at 25 °C. Use a HC PL APO CS2 63×/1.2 water objective with 1.5× optical zoom. Set pinhole to 1 airy unit, scan speed to 400 Hz unidirectional, acquire 512 × 512 pixels (8‑bit) → pixel size 241 nm × 241 nm, image field 123 µm × 123 µm. Excite with 488 nm (10 % of white laser) and 574 nm (5 % of white laser) lines, hybrid detectors, 2× line averaging, white laser power at 70 %. Set Z‑stack interval to 0.75 µm, collect 10–20 stacks to cover the entire germarium, yielding a temporal resolution of 30–60 s per stack. Plan a time‑lapse up to 3 h (optional multiple fields).

steps.title: Locate germarium and start acquisition
steps.instruction: Using bright‑field, locate a flat‑lying germarium on the glass. Switch to fluorescence to identify GSCs (anterior position, larger diffuse nuclei) and niche cells (compact nuclei). Ensure niche orientation is orthogonal to the GSCs. Begin the time‑lapse acquisition as configured.

steps.title: Process images in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open movies with Fiji’s Bio‑Formats Importer, view as a Hyperstack in Composite mode. Adjust brightness, then apply an exponential‑fit bleach correction. Apply a 3D Gaussian blur with 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 pixel kernel. Generate a maximum‑intensity projection of the Z‑stack (e.g., first 10 slices of an 18‑slice movie). Crop the projection to the region of interest using Ctrl + Shift + X. Measure projection length with the line tool (Analyze → Measure). Save the final movie as an .avi file at the desired frame rate (e.g., 5 fps or 15 fps).

steps.title: Measure projections and export
steps.instruction: For each projection, draw a line along its length, record the measurement, and repeat for all structures of interest. Export the processed movies as .avi files (commonly 5 fps for 1 min intervals or 15 fps for 45 s intervals).
